track.title: Segah
track.notes: Same audio as 'Ahmad Ebadi, Setar Solo' (2000), CD1 track 5 (Segah I), sample-aligned; that release is not analysed separately.

just_intervals.note: measured octave minus 1200 ¢, register to register

progression.narrative: The performance opens on Dk4 and dwells most on Eb in Phrase 1. Phrase 3 (0:17.8) introduces Dk, Ak, centred on Eb. Phrase 7 (0:56.7) introduces Gk, centred on F. Phrase 10 (1:29.5) introduces Ab, centred on F. Phrase 11 (1:40.7) introduces Bb, centred on Gk. The line peaks at C5 (546.8 Hz) at 2:17.5. It closes on Eb4, not the tonic (Ak4 → Ak4 → F4 → F4 → Eb4 → Eb4).

theory_fit.name: Pythagorean / Safi al-Din
theory_fit.description: Nearest note of the 17-note gamut generated by pure fifths (±8) from the tonic.

theory_fit.name: Farhat interval classes
theory_fit.description: Interval classes Hormoz Farhat measured in performance practice ("The Dastgah Concept in Persian Music", 1990). Approximate centres.

flags: tonic Dk set in the catalog (Segah's finalis, about D +1 cent (146.9 Hz): the pitch set fits Segah 7 of 7 from it (142, 348, 490, 632/699, 848, 1050 cents), as in his Segah on 'Setar' (2009, D +14). The vote picked the 2nd above, mostly a passing tone in Segah (Farhat 1990, p. 51). Inference, not yet by ear); the runs' vote favoured 318.1 Hz (Ek)
